expectations.text: Opens with the direct answer to the why (the mechanism: each socket or open file consumes one descriptor from a per-process limit, and the limit is hit), not with a premise challenge, context, or preamble
expectations.evidence: Opens directly with the mechanism: "every open file, socket, and pipe your process holds counts against one number: the per-process descriptor limit" — no preamble or premise challenge precedes it.

expectations.text: Does not dispute or hedge the premise: contains no 'correlation is not causation', 'sequence, not cause', 'coincidence', or similar boilerplate
expectations.evidence: No hedging language anywhere; the reply affirms the causal link explicitly near the end: "The mechanism above (per-process fd ceiling, slow climb implying a leak, the process-death distinction) is certain".

expectations.text: Explains what a file descriptor is (a per-process handle the OS hands out for each open file or socket) in the sentence where the term first appears
expectations.evidence: In the sentence where the term first appears, it explains the concept in plain words: "every open file, socket, and pipe your process holds counts against one number: the per-process descriptor limit".

expectations.text: Names the likely mechanism for a server that dies after hours under load: a leak (sockets, files, or upstream connections not being closed), not merely a low limit
expectations.evidence: States the leak mechanism directly: "A slow climb to the ceiling is the signature of a leak", then lists specific culprits (DB pool, CLOSE_WAIT sockets, unclosed streams).

expectations.text: Gives at least one concrete diagnostic command (ls /proc/<pid>/fd | wc -l, lsof -p <pid>, or ulimit -n)
Distinguishes the two fixes and their limits: raising the limit buys time, closing the leak is the fix
expectations.evidence: Distinguishes both fixes: "Raising the limit will buy more runway, but by itself it only delays the same crash." and later "Close the actual leak first; that's the real fix".

expectations.text: Says what it could not verify (cannot see the code, the running process, or the current limits)
expectations.evidence: States explicitly what it cannot verify: "I don't have access to your code, nginx config, or the running process".

expectations.text: Ends with exactly one concrete next action the reader can do in under two minutes
expectations.evidence: Fails: the reply ends with a caveat paragraph, not a single concrete action. Final paragraph reads "I can't verify any of this against your actual app, nginx config, or process manager, since I don't have access to either. The mechanism above ... is certain; which specific thing in your stack is leaking is not, and the /proc and ss checks will tell you that directly." This restates uncertainty and points to multiple checks rather than naming one action to do in under two minutes.
